$comment: PROGRAMME INTEGRATION LEDGER -- the repository's own record of who owns what,
which global application versions are spoken for, and which integration
baselines are current.
WHY IT EXISTS. Until 18 Sep 2026 every one of these facts lived only in prose
that a session had to read and remember. It failed in practice, twice in one
day and in opposite directions: the Quran stream claimed v08.26 was on `main`
while it was on a branch, and two independent builds simultaneously carried
08.27 -- exactly the thing a version number exists to prevent. Neither was
caught by any guard; both were caught by a person reading carefully.
HOW TO USE IT. This file is DATA, not authority. It records decisions the
Master Architect has made; it does not make them. `tools/i18n-verify/
programme-ledger.mjs` reads it and fails when the repository and this record
disagree. Editing this file to silence a guard, without the decision behind
it, is the one way it can do harm.
VERSION FORM. Every version in a DATA field is canonical bare `NN.NN` -- the
form `app/js/version.js` itself stores. Prose refers to them as `vNN.NN`.
Guard D exists because a version named in the brief ONLY in bare form is
invisible to every v-prefixed scanner in the repository, which is how
`CLAUDE.md`'s own forward allocation of 08.28 went unseen while another
stream consumed it.
baselineSha is the tip `main` stood at when this record was last written.
`main` moves forward constantly and that is not drift, so the guard asserts
baselineSha is an ANCESTOR of origin/main rather than equal to it, and
reports the distance. A baselineSha that is NOT an ancestor means history
was rewritten or the record names a commit from somewhere else -- that is a
hard failure.

streams.activeBranchNote: NULL DELIBERATELY -- the repair of 19 Sep 2026, and the reason is recorded here rather than left to be rediscovered. `feature/hadith-study` still exists and is still where Hadith test/documentation work is prepared, but it TRACKS main: it carries no version stamp of its own, and its app/js/version.js is whatever main's is. An `activeBranch` in this ledger means 'a branch this stream stamps, whose stamp the guards cross-check against declaredVersion'. Naming it while it tracked main made guard A read main's own stamp as a Hadith disagreement and guard B read it as an invented version -- both artefacts of the record, not of the branch. Positive and negative tests against the real guard established that `declaredVersion: null` ALONE does NOT clear A and B, that declaring main's number would falsely claim the Quran stream's allocation, and that a null activeBranch is the only truthful representation this schema supports. COST, reported rather than discovered later: guards A, B and guard E's live branch-diff sweep all skip a stream with no activeBranch, so an undeclared shared-file modification on this branch would not be caught by that sweep. Mitigated, not ignored: this stream is MERGED_TO_MAIN with nothing unmerged left to oversee, and guard E still validates and reports all five of its authorization RECORDS, which it reads from the records themselves rather than from a branch diff. Set this field again, with a declaredVersion the Master Architect has allocated, on the day this stream next stamps a version. SECOND COST, measured rather than predicted: programme-ledger-mutations.mjs's guard-A mutation "the ledger and the branch disagree about what the branch is stamped" hard-codes the stream id "hadith", so with no activeBranch here guard A skips it and the mutation is a no-op -- it reports UNPROVEN, and the suite exits 1. Guard A's three other failure modes remained proven throughout. RESOLVED THE SAME DAY: it was raised as SHARED CHANGE REQUEST SCR-HADITH-02, the Master Architect AUTHORIZED it separately, and the fix is APPLIED -- the mutation derives its subject stream from the ledger (l.streams.find(x => x.activeBranch && f.branches[x.activeBranch])), exactly as guard B's two mutations already do, so it cannot go stale on this stream again; the suite is back to 49/0 and its intended failure was re-measured rather than assumed. See docs/reports/2026-09-19-hadith-scr02-mutation-fix.md. The guard A / guard B / guard E skipping described above is unchanged, and is still the standing cost of a null activeBranch.
streams.branchTipNote: The commit at which this stream's work reached `main` -- not a moving branch tip. branchTip is read by guard C only for an integrationState of HELD, so for a merged stream it is descriptive. Re-stamping it with the branch's own newest commit would name the very commit that wrote the stamp, and would move again every time the branch merged main: an endless self-reference. This commit never moves. The branch's pre-repair tip was c1a4f19a70ec824372fa1fda49e4e7dbc38bc40c.

sharedChangeRequests.currentOwnerUse: Platform/shared behaviour verification for every module and page.
requiredChange: behaviour.mjs accumulates module-specific exclusions for elements that are
intentionally multilingual or multiscript (Arabic source text, transliteration,
narrator names). Each module adds its own exclusion, so the shared file grows a
module-shaped list that no module owns.
reason: The replacement is a SEMANTIC DECLARATIVE CONTRACT -- an element declares what it
IS (source scripture, transliteration, proper name) and the suite derives whether
it should be translated. That is distinct from `data-i18n-skip`, which declares
only that a check should not look, and carries no meaning a second consumer
sharedChangeRequests.expectedBlastRadius: BR-1 or above -- it touches markup across every module's pages and the shared suite.
sharedChangeRequests.decision: DEFERRED. Recorded as accepted architectural debt. NOT authorised for implementation.

designRecords.subject: Cross-module behaviour verification structure
record: behaviour.mjs is one monolithic file, now 56 sections and 982 checks, verifying
every module. Each new module grows it. The longer-term candidate direction is
module-specific behaviour suites plus a thin aggregate runner that composes them
and reports one total -- rather than unlimited growth of one file.
This is a DIRECTION, not a decision, and nothing in this tranche implements it.
It is recorded so the next platform round does not rediscover the problem, and
so no module round quietly splits the file on its own authority.

repository's GitHub Pages site serves `main`, so code merged to main IS
served from the live URL even while the feature cannot function. One
boolean cannot carry both facts, and collapsing them is how a control the
Owner can actually see gets recorded as 'not deployed'. Master Architect
correction, 2026-09-19.

four states ever to become true. The separation the correction above
made is exactly why this could be recorded precisely: Rules ARE
deployed now, but evidenceRecordingOperational stays NO on purpose --
a second, GOVERNED decision (Phase 4 activation), deliberately not made
in the same step as the Rules publish. Conflating the two would have
been the same class of error this file was created to stop.
